claims.name: observable-equivalence ceiling
assumptions: the competing hypotheses induce identical probability measures on the complete allowed transcript space
nonclaims: does not imply restricted simulator models are untestable
Bayes factors on zero-probability events are not assigned the value one

claims.name: shared-latent representational refinement invariance
assumptions: clone weights sum to the parent weight
clone conditional observable laws are identical
the refinement is representational rather than the physical creation of additional measure-bearing observers
nonclaims: does not identify a privileged anthropic measure
does not say physically creating new conscious observers leaves observer measure unchanged

claims.name: rational refinement-additive uniqueness
assumptions: local rule depends only on rational probability weight
finite split additivity for nonnegative rational weights
nonclaims: not claimed as mathematically novel
does not cover observer measures using additional physical or phenomenal structure

claims.name: persistent-latent likelihood-ratio identity and ceiling
claims.status: elementary finite-mixture identity applied to hierarchical sampling
assumptions: one latent component is drawn once and persists through the transcript
the two compared hypotheses share conditional transcript laws and differ only in component weights
for the displayed pointwise mass/density formula the transcript is discrete or all component laws are dominated by one common sigma-finite measure
component-level absolute continuity holds on the realized support: the denominator gives positive weight to every component contributing positive numerator likelihood
nonclaims: does not prevent a long transcript from identifying the active component
does not apply unchanged when the hypotheses also differ in within-component transcript laws
does not give a finite ceiling across support mismatch
does not assert a pointwise density formula for arbitrary mutually singular component families without a declared dominating representation

claims.name: known-channel affine-rank identification
assumptions: the observation channel K is a known channel
finite latent and observed alphabets
nonclaims: not claimed as novel
does not address joint unknown prior/channel identification

failure of point identification does not make Bayesian analysis impossible; it calls for explicit prior sensitivity, identified sets, or robust posterior ranges rather than data-unique point certainty

claims.name: row-stochastic one-view factorization gauge
assumptions: A is invertible, nonnegative, and row-stochastic
the transformed prior pi A^{-1} remains nonnegative
nonclaims: does not classify all latent-factorization nonuniqueness
does not imply every unknown prior/channel model has this exact gauge
a genuine local continuum additionally needs an interior prior and a nontrivial row-stochastic perturbation that changes K

claims.name: same-channel repeated-view rigidity inside the row-stochastic gauge
assumptions: K has full row rank
both observations use the same channel K
the observations are conditionally independent given the same persistent latent
A is invertible, nonnegative, and row-stochastic
pi A^{-1} is strictly positive
the repeated shared-latent two-view law is preserved
nonclaims: not unrestricted two-view latent-class identifiability
does not establish the analogous result for two different view-specific channels
does not remove latent ambiguities outside the declared gauge
strict positivity and full row rank are substantive assumptions
